title: Discovery and account-console interactions each emit one structured audit event on the fixed allow-list
asA: operator running the runtime-verify suite against the discovery client and the account-console verification
iWant: every named interaction on those two families to write one structured event carrying only the allow-list fields
soThat: the audit stream stays free of token material and a reviewer can decide at a glance whether an event field is inside the blueprint's contract

acceptanceCriteria.description: A completed discovery fetch for realm `alpha` emits exactly one `keycloak.discovery` audit event carrying `family=keycloak.discovery`, `outcome=verified`, `realmSlug=alpha`, and `at`; no other field appears.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm-config record for `alpha` whose issuer is reachable and whose discovery document responds 200
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client fetches the realm's OIDC discovery document at boot
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one event whose own-property keys are exactly `{family, outcome, realmSlug, at}` with `family=keycloak.discovery` and `outcome=verified`; no token value, no client secret, no raw claim record, and no substring of any of the above appears in any field

acceptanceCriteria.description: A refused account-console verification emits exactly one `keycloak.account_console` audit event carrying `outcome=refused` and a `reasonClass` value.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm-config record for `alpha` whose `accountConsoleUrl` returns 404 to an unauthenticated GET
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client verifies the account console URL at boot
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one event whose own-property keys are exactly `{family, outcome, reasonClass, realmSlug, at}` with `family=keycloak.account_console` and `outcome=refused`; the reasonClass value is a stable-coded string; no token value, no client secret, no raw claim record, and no substring of any of the above appears in any field

acceptanceCriteria.description: A transient discovery failure followed by a successful retry emits exactly one refusal event and one verified event on the `keycloak.discovery` family, in order.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm-config record for `alpha` whose discovery endpoint returns 503 on the first attempt and 200 on the second
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client retries per its documented retry posture and completes the fetch
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly two events in order: one `keycloak.discovery` event with `outcome=refused` and `reasonClass=upstream_unavailable`, then one `keycloak.discovery` event with `outcome=verified`; no additional event is written for the retry itself

acceptanceCriteria.description: A sink failure during the emission of a `keycloak.discovery` event does not mask the underlying discovery outcome; the mechanism records a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event and the discovery outcome is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a realm-config record for `alpha` whose discovery responds 200 and an audit sink whose write throws
acceptanceCriteria.when: the discovery client emits the completion event
acceptanceCriteria.then: the discovery outcome remains `verified` (boot proceeds); the mechanism records a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event carrying the realm slug and a reason-class string; no token value or raw claim record appears; the original refusal or verification result is not masked
